_comment: Single source of truth for the project tagging taxonomy. Edit this file to add/remove features, change descriptions, or tune rules. The Python script reads this at startup and builds the prompt + CSV headers from it automatically.

features._comment: Scored 0-5 per project. 0=absent, 1=weak signal, 2=minor, 3=explicitly required but not central, 4=clearly required, 5=defining feature. Only non-zero values are returned by the LLM (sparse).

application_types._comment: Binary (0 or 1). A project may belong to multiple types simultaneously. Only 1s are returned (sparse).

definitions.website: Primarily informational or content-based, not a full interactive application.
definitions.web_application: Interactive software running in a browser.
definitions.marketplace: Multiple buyers/sellers or service providers transacting with each other.
definitions.api_backend: Primary deliverable is an API or backend service, not a UI.
definitions.other: Use only if none of the above types fit.

technology_modifiers._comment: Binary (0 or 1). Tag only when the project explicitly mentions or clearly requires this platform. Only 1s are returned (sparse).

numeric_modifiers._comment: Always return all keys. Use 0 only if truly none detectable — always estimate when the project implies a value.

fields.external_api_count: How many distinct external APIs or third-party services does this project integrate? Count each distinct service as 1 (e.g. Stripe + Twilio + Google Maps = 3).
fields.estimated_screens: How many distinct UI screens or pages does this project likely have? Estimate based on described features and application type.
fields.estimated_entities: How many distinct data entities need full CRUD operations? (e.g. User, Product, Order each count as 1)

boolean_modifiers._comment: Binary (0 or 1). Always return all keys.

fields.real_time: Does it require real-time updates — websockets, live data feeds, or push notifications?
fields.mobile: Does it need a native or hybrid mobile app (iOS and/or Android)?
fields.web: Does it need a web interface (browser-based UI)?
fields.offline: Does it need to work without an internet connection (offline-first)?
fields.legacy_system: Does it involve integrating with or maintaining a legacy system?
fields.existing_codebase: Does it require working on an existing codebase rather than starting from scratch?
fields.requires_refactoring: Does it explicitly require refactoring or restructuring existing code?
fields.requires_reverse_engineering: Does it require reverse engineering an existing system, API, or undocumented behavior?
fields.cross_platform: Does it need to run across multiple platforms (e.g. iOS + Android, or web + desktop)?

enum_modifiers._comment: Always return all keys. Pick exactly one value from the allowed list for each field.

project_type.description: Overall nature of the work being requested.

ai_level.description: none=no AI involved, basic=simple AI API call (e.g. ChatGPT wrapper), advanced=custom model training, fine-tuning, or complex ML pipeline.

business_logic.description: How much complex domain-specific business logic does this project contain? low=mostly CRUD, medium=some workflows or rules, high=complex domain logic, pricing engines, multi-step workflows.

data_volume.description: Expected scale of data the system will handle. small=hundreds to thousands of records, medium=tens to hundreds of thousands, large=millions+ or big data processing.

integration_complexity.description: How complex are the external integrations? low=0-1 simple APIs, medium=2-4 APIs or one complex integration, high=5+ integrations or deeply coupled third-party systems.

ui_complexity.description: How complex is the user interface? low=simple forms and lists, medium=custom components or moderate interactivity, high=complex dashboards, drag-and-drop, data-heavy visualizations.

algorithmic_complexity.description: How algorithmically demanding is the core logic? low=standard CRUD and routing, medium=moderate computation or optimization, high=heavy computation, simulations, advanced algorithms, or real-time processing.

prompt_rules._comment: These rules are injected verbatim into the LLM system prompt under a 'Rules' section. Edit here to tune model behavior without touching the Python.
rules: Return ALL projects in the batch, in the same order.
For features, ONLY include keys with value >= 1 (omit 0s to save tokens).
For application_type and technology_modifiers, ONLY include keys with value 1.
For numeric, boolean, and enum modifiers, ALWAYS include all keys.
When tagging projects with existing_codebase=1, only tag features that are to be ADDED or MODIFIED, not the entire feature set of the existing codebase.
Omit features that come pre-installed with the technology platform (e.g. admin panels in WordPress).
Be strict — do not make assumptions that are unlikely given the project description.
A project may belong to MULTIPLE application types simultaneously.
Return raw JSON only — no markdown fences, no explanation text.

If a feature is scored ≥4, verify that at least one corresponding application_type is also set to 1 while keeping the feature in features list (e.g. Bots & Automation ≥4 → automation_system; Payment Processing ≥4 → financial_system or ecommerce; Booking & Reservation ≥4 → booking_system).
